title: Qbar-l proper base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and let
$K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$. The descended exchange transformation of
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] is an isomorphism
$$
 Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',\Qlb).
$$
If $K$ is represented by a pair $(E,K_E)$ with $K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$, this map
is represented after a finite overfield $M$ by the $M$-coefficient exchange
isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-finite-extension] applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$. The
result is independent of $E$, $M$, and the representative.

note:
*Source note:* at each finite stage this is Stacks Project, Pro-etale
Cohomology, Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag
09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)), applied with
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$: a proper base-change isomorphism for a derived
complete $K$ whose reductions are bounded below and of etale origin. What
the blueprint adds is the statement on the $\Qlb$ coefficient category
$\Dbc(Y',\Qlb)$, obtained by descent from the finite-stage isomorphisms
along the scalar extensions $T_{F/E}$, together with the independence of the
stage and of the representative.

proof.text: Properness is stable under the specified Cartesian base change. Apply actual-coefficient constructible preservation on identity-horizontal squares for the two proper direct images; finite dimensionality of proper fibers supplies the bound, and the canonical DVR uniformizer kills l in the first coefficient quotient. Use the recorded integral completed-pullback preservation for the other two operations.

Apply pbcDescentOperations to these four preservation witnesses. It returns exactly the four canonically normalized coherent families and compatible localized actual exchange required by the presentation.

For every finite coefficient field and integral representative, compare actual completed exchange with strict completed exchange. The complete-pro-etale theorem makes the latter invertible, since the integral stage retains intrinsic completeness and compatible etale origins. Reflect invertibility through the full-subcategory inclusion and preserve it through scalar localization. The specified heterogeneous equality and the four finite-stage functor equalities identify the resulting isomorphism with the presentation exchange component.

The generic stage-system isomorphism-of-descent theorem and composition isomorphisms give descended invertibility. Generic proved stage-inclusion and beta-compatibility identities give the finite-overfield formula. Naturality gives representative-isomorphism independence. The two presentation definitions factor through exactly these generic constructions, with their original formulas and unchanged mathematical values.

proof_origin.place: Actual coefficient preservation, strict-tower exchange comparison, and the existing generic stage-system descent formulas. Unit-level proper-base-change route unchanged.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
and a prime $\ell\neq p$, and use Weil sheaves and Weil complexes with
coefficients $\Lambda=\Qlb$ as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'_0 & \xrightarrow{\;h'_0\;} & X_0\\
{\scriptstyle f'_0}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle f_0}\\
Y'_0 & \xrightarrow{\;h_0\;} & Y_0
\end{array}
$$

be a cartesian square of $k_0$-schemes with $f_0$ proper and $h_0$ arbitrary,
where $Y_0$ and $Y'_0$ are of finite type over $k_0$
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]). Write $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and
similarly $X'$, $Y$, $Y'$, for the geometric fibres, $f,f',h,h'$ for the
induced morphisms (again a cartesian square, with $f$ and $f'$ proper), and
$g_X,g_{X'},g_Y,g_{Y'}$ for the geometric Frobenius automorphisms of
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed], which commute with $f,f',h,h'$.

On Weil modules, the pullback $h^*(M,\theta)$ is the module pullback $h^*M$
([det-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]) with the Weil structure
$g_{Y'}^*h^*M\cong h^*g_Y^*M\xrightarrow{h^*\theta}h^*M$, and the pushforward
$f_*(M,\theta)$ is $f_*M$ with the Weil structure
$g_Y^*f_*M\cong f_*g_X^*M\xrightarrow{f_*\theta}f_*M$ (the first isomorphism
holds because $g_X,g_Y$ are automorphisms with $fg_X=g_Yf$); likewise for
$h'$ and $f'$. Write $h^*$ for the functor induced by the exact pullback on
derived categories of Weil modules, and $Rf_*$ for the right derived functor
of the pushforward.

1. For every Weil complex $K$ on $X_0$, the objects $h^*Rf_*K$ and
   $Rf'_*h'^*K$ are Weil complexes on $Y'_0$, and the base change morphism
   $$
   \mathrm{BC}_K\colon h^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_*h'^*K,
   $$
   formed by the formula of [sk-def-sfb-base-change-morphism] from the
   derived adjunctions $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $f'^*\dashv Rf'_*$ of Weil modules
   and the pullback comparison $f'^*h^*\cong h'^*f^*$, is an isomorphism of
   Weil complexes.
2. For every Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ and every $i\geq0$, with
   $R^if_*\mathcal F=\mathcal H^i(Rf_*\mathcal F)$, there is an isomorphism of
   Weil sheaves on $Y'_0$
   $$
   h^*R^if_*\mathcal F\cong R^if'_*h'^*\mathcal F .
   $$

proof.text:
*Forgetting the Weil structure.* Let $\operatorname{For}$ denote the forgetful
functor from Weil modules to modules, and also the induced functor on derived
categories ([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]). The unit and counit of the module
adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ commute with the Weil structures defined in the
statement (they are natural and compatible with the composition isomorphisms
for $fg_X=g_Yf$), so $f^*\dashv f_*$ lifts to Weil modules, and likewise for
$f'$; $\operatorname{For}$ carries these adjunctions, and the pullback
comparison, to the module ones. On Weil modules over $T$, $\operatorname{For}$
has the exact left adjoint $M\mapsto\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}(g_T^n)^*M$, with
the Weil structure permuting the summands, so $\operatorname{For}$ preserves
K-injective complexes. As it commutes with the underived $f_*$, it follows that
$\operatorname{For}\circ Rf_*\cong Rf_*\circ\operatorname{For}$, compatibly
with units and counits, and trivially $\operatorname{For}\circ h^*=
h^*\circ\operatorname{For}$. Hence
$\operatorname{For}(\mathrm{BC}_K)$ is the base change morphism
$\mathrm{BC}_{\operatorname{For}K}$ of [sk-def-sfb-base-change-morphism] for
the square $X',X,Y',Y$ over $k$ and $\operatorname{For}K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$.

*Constructibility and the isomorphism.* The schemes $X,X',Y,Y'$ are of finite
type over $k$, and $Y,Y'$ are quasi-compact. Both assertions below are local on
$Y$, resp. $Y'$: restriction to an open subscheme commutes with derived direct
images ([Tag 0D6G](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D6G)), with inverse
images, units and counits, hence carries $\mathrm{BC}$ to the base change
morphism of the restricted square. Cover $Y$ by finitely many affine opens
$V$, and $Y'$ by finitely many affine opens $V'$ each mapping into some
affine open $V$ of $Y$; then $V,V'$, and $f^{-1}V$,
$f'^{-1}V'$ (proper over them), are separated and of finite type over $k$.
Inverse images and, for $\Lambda=\Qlb$, direct images preserve bounded
constructible complexes between such schemes ([sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors];
for the proper direct images also [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational]
(2)). Applying this on the finitely many affine opens involved,
$Rf_*\operatorname{For}K$, $h^*Rf_*\operatorname{For}K$ and
$Rf'_*h'^*\operatorname{For}K$ are bounded with constructible cohomology; since
$\operatorname{For}$ commutes with $Rf_*$, $Rf'_*$, $h^*$, $h'^*$ and with
cohomology objects, $h^*Rf_*K$ and $Rf'_*h'^*K$ are Weil complexes. By
[det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational] (3) for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ and the
restricted squares, $\mathrm{BC}_{\operatorname{For}K}=
\operatorname{For}(\mathrm{BC}_K)$ is an isomorphism. A morphism of complexes
of Weil modules is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if the underlying morphism
of complexes of modules is one, since cohomology of Weil modules is computed
on the underlying modules; so $\mathrm{BC}_K$ is an isomorphism, and it is an
isomorphism of Weil complexes because these form a full subcategory of the
derived category of Weil modules. This proves (1).

*Weil sheaves.* Apply (1) to $K=\mathcal F[0]$. The pullbacks $h^*$, $h'^*$ are
induced by exact functors of Weil modules, so they commute with
$\mathcal H^i$ and $h'^*(\mathcal F[0])=(h'^*\mathcal F)[0]$. Taking
$\mathcal H^i$ of $\mathrm{BC}_{\mathcal F[0]}$ gives
$h^*R^if_*\mathcal F\cong R^if'_*h'^*\mathcal F$ as Weil sheaves, which is (2).

lean.statement: theorem qbar_properBaseChange [IsProper f] : ∃ P : PbcQbarExchangePresentation l Ω sq, (∀ K : pbcQbarCategory l Ω X, IsIso ((P.exchange).app K)) ∧ (∀ (M : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω) (K : pbcStageCategory l Ω X M), IsIso ((P.Ex.τ M).app K)) ∧ (∀ (K : pbcQbarCategory l Ω X) (M : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω) (h : K.stage ≤ M), (P.exchange).app K = PbcQbarExchangePresentation.atStage l Ω sq P K M h) ∧ (∀ (K L : pbcQbarCategory l Ω X) (h : K ≅ L), (P.Rf.base.functor ⋙ P.Lg.base.functor).map h.hom ≫ (P.exchange).app L = (P.exchange).app K ≫ (P.Lg'.base.functor ⋙ P.Rf'.base.functor).map h.hom)
